docs.text: HardFOC driver PCA9685 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the NXP PCA9685 16-channel, 12-bit PWM controller. It sets the PWM frequency, drives each channel by duty cycle or by on/off tick, and controls sleep and the output stage, on any MCU with I2C. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that brings an I2C bus up and reads and writes register bytes; it does the rest: the prescaler calculation, the sleep sequence the PRE_SCALE register needs, channel frames, retries and error flags. 16-channel, 12-bit PWM LED controller PCA9685 NXP Semiconductors Outputs 16 channels, 12-bit (4096 steps) each, with a programmable on time and off time PWM frequency 24 Hz to 1526 Hz, one frequency for all channels (25 MHz internal oscillator, or EXTCLK up to 50 MHz) Host interface I2C up to 1 MHz (Fast-mode Plus); 7-bit address 0x40 to 0x7F from pins A0 to A5 Output stage Totem pole (25 mA sink, 10 mA source at 5 V) or open drain; OE pin, active low Supply 2.3 V to 5.5 V, inputs and outputs 5.5 V tolerant; −40 °C to +85 °C Package TSSOP28, HVQFN28 Datasheet (Rev. 4) What you get ¶ One object per chip. PCA9685<YourBus> takes the bus and the 7-bit address; several chips share one bus. See API guide . Frequency in hertz. SetPwmFreq() computes PRE_SCALE and runs the sleep / write / wake sequence the chip requires. See PWM timing . Channels by duty or by tick. SetDuty() , SetPwm() with a phase offset, full on, full off and all channels at once. See API guide . Errors you can inspect. Every call returns bool ; a bitmask of Error flags says why. Register accesses retry with an optional delay. See API guide . Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class with three methods: no virtual calls, no heap, no RTOS dependency. See Porting . Tested without hardware. Host unit tests run the driver against a model of the chip's registers. See Testing and CI . API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: initialise, set the frequency, drive outputs, configure the output stage, sleep and handle errors. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with Driver standing for pca9685::PCA9685<MyI2c> . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One PCA9685<I2cType> object per chip, constructed with a pointer to your port and the chip's 7-bit address. Every call that touches the chip is noexcept and returns bool . Task Calls Start up EnsureInitialized() , Reset() , IsInitialized() Frequency SetPwmFreq(float hz) , GetPrescale(uint8_t&) One channel SetDuty(ch, duty) , SetPwm(ch, on, off) , SetChannelFullOn(ch) , SetChannelFullOff(ch) All channels SetAllPwm(on, off) Output stage SetOutputDriverMode(bool totem_pole) , SetOutputInvert(bool invert) , SetOutputEnable(bool enable) Power Sleep() , Wake() Errors GetErrorFlags() , HasError(e) , HasAnyError() , ClearError(e) , ClearErrorFlags(mask) , GetLastError() Bus robustness SetRetries(int) , SetRetryDelay(void (*)()) Version GetDriverVersion() , GetDriverVersionMajor() , GetDriverVersionMinor() , GetDriverVersionPatch() Channels are 0 to 15 ( MAX_CHANNELS_ = 16 ); ticks are 0 to 4095 ( MAX_PWM_ ). Initialise ¶ Driver pwm ( & bus , 0x40 ); pwm . SetRetries ( 2 ); // up to 3 attempts per register access pwm . SetRetryDelay ([] { platform_delay_ms ( 1 ); }); // between attempts: let the bus recover if ( ! pwm . EnsureInitialized ()) { // bus up, then MODE1 = 0x20 (oscillator on, AI) return false ; } EnsureInitialized() brings your bus up and writes MODE1 = 0x20 : oscillator on, register auto-increment on (MODE1.AI, which the four-byte channel writes need), sub-addresses and All Call off. Every other call runs it on first use, so this step is optional, but calling it at start-up reports a wiring problem where you can act on it. Reset() writes MODE1 again at any time; it does not touch the channel registers, MODE2 or PRE_SCALE. Set the frequency ¶ if ( ! pwm . SetPwmFreq ( 1000.0f )) { // 24 .. 1526 Hz, same for all 16 channels return false ; // Error::OutOfRange outside that range } uint8_t prescale = 0 ; if ( ! pwm . GetPrescale ( prescale )) { // 1000 Hz -> PRE_SCALE = 5 return false ; } const float actual_hz = 25'000'000.0f / ( 4096.0f * ( prescale + 1 )); // 1017 Hz std :: printf ( "PWM %.0f Hz (prescale %u) 
 " , static_cast < double > ( actual_hz ), prescale ); One frequency serves all 16 channels. The chip only accepts a new PRE_SCALE while asleep, so SetPwmFreq() briefly stops the oscillator and every output; call it once at start-up, not in a loop. PWM timing has the formula and a table of common frequencies. Drive the outputs ¶ if ( ! pwm . SetDuty ( 0 , 0.25f )) { // channel 0: high for the first 25 % of the period return false ; } if ( ! pwm . SetPwm ( 1 , 1024 , 3072 )) { // channel 1: 50 %, rising at tick 1024 (phase shift) return false ; } if ( ! pwm . SetChannelFullOn ( 2 ) || ! pwm . SetChannelFullOff ( 3 )) { // 2 constantly high, 3 constantly low return false ; } return pwm . SetAllPwm ( 0 , 2048 ); // all 16 channels: 50 %, overrides the above Call Use it for SetDuty(ch, duty) LED brightness, motor speed: duty from 0.0 to 1.0, clamped, rising edge at tick 0; 0.0 is full off, 1.0 full on SetPwm(ch, on, off) Exact pulse widths (servos) and phase-shifted channels SetChannelFullOn(ch) , SetChannelFullOff(ch) A constant high or low, with no PWM edges SetAllPwm(on, off) The same value on all 16 channels in one write For a servo, compute ticks from the pulse width: // Servo pulse width to PWM ticks: one period is 4096 ticks of 1 / f_pwm. bool set_servo_us ( Driver & pwm , uint8_t channel , float pulse_us , float pwm_hz ) { const float period_us = 1'000'000.0f / pwm_hz ; // 20 000 us at 50 Hz const auto ticks = static_cast < uint16_t > ( pulse_us / period_us * 4096.0f + 0.5f ); return pwm . SetPwm ( channel , 0 , ticks ); // 1500 us at 50 Hz -> 307 ticks } Configure the output stage ¶ if ( ! pwm . SetOutputDriverMode ( false )) { // MODE2.OUTDRV = 0: open-drain (sink only) return false ; } return pwm . SetOutputInvert ( true ); // MODE2.INVRT = 1: for LEDs wired to VDD The power-up default is totem pole, not inverted: right for servo signals and logic inputs. Use open drain for LEDs with built-in Zener diodes, and inversion for LEDs wired from VDD to the pin. Hardware has the MODE2 bits. With OE wired to a GPIO, SetOutputEnable() blanks or enables all 16 outputs at once through your port's GpioSet() ( Porting ); it sends nothing on the bus: pwm . SetOutputEnable ( false ); // OE high: all outputs blanked (MODE2.OUTNE state) if ( ! pwm . SetAllPwm ( 0 , 2048 )) { // program the channels while blanked return false ; } return pwm . SetOutputEnable ( true ); // OE low: outputs follow their registers Sleep and wake ¶ if ( ! pwm . Sleep ()) { // MODE1.SLEEP = 1: oscillator off, outputs stop return false ; } // ... low-power period ... return pwm . Wake (); // SLEEP = 0, 500 us start-up, then RESTART Sleep() sets MODE1.SLEEP: the oscillator stops, the outputs stop and the chip draws 2.2 µA typical. The channel registers keep their values. Wake() follows the restart procedure of section 7.3.1.1: it clears SLEEP, waits the 500 µs oscillator start-up time and then, when the chip set RESTART on the way into sleep, writes RESTART to resume every channel where it was. When Wake() returns, output timing is valid again. The wait goes through your port's optional DelayUs() ( Porting ). Handle errors ¶ if ( ! pwm . SetPwm ( 16 , 0 , 100 )) { // channel 16 does not exist if ( pwm . HasError ( Driver :: Error :: OutOfRange )) { std :: printf ( "bad argument 
 " ); } if ( pwm . HasError ( Driver :: Error :: I2cWrite ) || pwm . HasError ( Driver :: Error :: I2cRead )) { std :: printf ( "bus failure after all retries 
 " ); } pwm . ClearErrorFlags (); // flags accumulate until you clear them } Flag Set when What to do Error::I2cWrite A write failed on every attempt, or the port's EnsureInitialized() failed Check wiring, pull-ups and address; see Troubleshooting Error::I2cRead A read failed on every attempt As above Error::OutOfRange Channel above 15, tick above 4095, frequency outside 24 Hz to 1526 Hz Fix the argument; nothing was sent Error::NotInitialized A call ran EnsureInitialized() and it failed Set together with the I2C flag that caused it InvalidParam and DeviceNotFound are declared but the driver never sets them. Flags accumulate across calls: read them, act, then clear them. Raw register access ¶ The driver keeps its register helpers private. For a register it has no call for (SUBADR1 to SUBADR3, ALLCALLADR, MODE2.OCH or OUTNE), write through your port directly, as one transaction: bus.Write(0x40, 0x01, &mode2, 1) . The register addresses are in the Register enum. Read MODE2 first and change only your bits: the driver's own MODE2 calls read-modify-write too, so the two stay consistent. docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: three layers, what each owns, and how one call reaches the chip. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one PCA9685 object, whose public calls (listed from inc/pca9685.hpp) set the frequency, the channels and the output stage. Each call turns into register reads and writes with retries. The communication interface (I2cInterface in inc/pca9685_i2c_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base that forwards them to your class. The platform port is the only code you write: a class that brings the I2C bus up and moves register bytes over it. Below it is the hardware. Drawn from: inc/pca9685.hpp PCA9685 public calls ; inc/pca9685_i2c_interface.hpp I2cInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The three layers ¶ Layer Where You change it when Hardware-agnostic core : PCA9685<I2cType> inc/pca9685.hpp , src/pca9685.ipp Never, for a new board Communication interface : I2cInterface<Derived> inc/pca9685_i2c_interface.hpp Never Platform port : your class, three methods Your project Once per MCU or board ( Porting ) Everything above the port is the same on ESP32, STM32, a Linux host or the unit-test model. That is how the host tests run the real driver code without hardware. How one call reaches the chip ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant D as PCA9685 core participant P as Your port participant C as PCA9685 chip A->>D: SetDuty(0, 0.075f) D->>D: clamp to 0..1, OFF = lround(0.075 x 4095) = 307 D->>D: EnsureInitialized() (first call only: Reset) D->>P: Write(0x40, LED0_ON_L, {00 00 33 01}, 4) P->>C: START, 0x40 + W, 0x06, 4 bytes, STOP C-->>P: ACK P-->>D: true (on NACK: false, retried up to SetRetries() times) D-->>A: true / false + Error flag Why CRTP ¶ The interface is a class template parameter, not a virtual base class. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: PCA9685<MyI2c> . Code that has to work with several port types takes the driver as a template parameter too. Lazy initialisation ¶ The constructor only stores the bus pointer and the address; it never touches the bus. The first call that needs the chip runs EnsureInitialized() , which calls the port's EnsureInitialized() and then Reset() (MODE1 = 0x00 ). After that, IsInitialized() is true and no call repeats it. Call EnsureInitialized() yourself at start-up to find wiring problems early, at a point where you can report them. Errors without exceptions ¶ Each call returns bool . On false , the reason is in two places: GetErrorFlags() : a bitmask of Error values that accumulates until you clear it with ClearErrorFlags() or ClearError() . GetLastError() : the most recent error; a later successful call sets it back to Error::None . Register accesses retry: one attempt plus SetRetries() more (3 by default), with an optional callback between attempts ( SetRetryDelay() ). docs.text: Changelog ¶ What changed in each release of the driver. Entries marked BREAKING need source changes in code that used the affected API. Unreleased ¶ Documentation ¶ The documentation site moved to the HardFOC MkDocs platform: new page set (quickstart, hardware, PWM timing, architecture, API guide, configuration, porting, examples, troubleshooting), the Doxygen API reference under /api/ , and every code sample compiled by the host build from tests/docs/ . Corrected the hardware facts: OE has no internal pull-up, the standby current is 2.2 µA typical (15.5 µA maximum), and 0x70 and 0x78 to 0x7F are not usable device addresses. Fixed ¶ Reset() / EnsureInitialized() now write MODE1 = 0x20 (AI = 1) instead of 0x00 , and every MODE1 write of the driver ( SetPwmFreq() , Sleep() , Wake() ) keeps AI set and never writes 1 to RESTART by accident. Without AI the register pointer does not advance, so the four-byte writes of SetPwm() , SetDuty() , SetAllPwm() , SetChannelFullOn() and SetChannelFullOff() only reached LEDn_ON_L (datasheet 7.3.1, Table 5). The auto-increment workaround is no longer needed. Wake() , SetPwmFreq() and Reset() now wait the 500 µs oscillator start-up time after clearing MODE1.SLEEP, and write RESTART only after it (datasheet Table 5 note 2, section 7.3.1.1). Wake() used to write RESTART at once and SetPwmFreq() never wrote it, so the channels did not resume after a frequency change. The wait uses the port's new optional DelayUs() hook, or MODE1 reads when the port has none. The "delay 500 µs after Wake() " workaround is no longer needed. SetDuty(ch, 0.0f) wrote ON = OFF = 0, and SetPwm() / SetAllPwm() passed equal ticks through, although LEDn_ON and LEDn_OFF must never hold the same count (datasheet 7.3.4). Equal ticks now write the full-OFF bit ( LEDn_OFF_H[4] ), and SetDuty(ch, 1.0f) sets the full-ON bit ( LEDn_ON_H[4] ) so that 100 % is constantly high instead of 4095 of 4096 ticks (7.3.3, Table 7). Use of SetChannelFullOn() / SetChannelFullOff() for the two ends is no longer needed. I2cInterface::GpioSetActive() and GpioSetInactive() called the base class's do-nothing GpioSet() , never the port's, so the OE hooks did nothing. They now dispatch to the port's GpioSet() (CRTP). cmake --install now produces a usable package: it installs src/pca9685.ipp (which pca9685.hpp includes) under include/hf_pca9685/src/ next to the headers in include/hf_pca9685/inc/ , and the exported target is hf::pca9685 , the same name as the in-tree alias (it was exported as hf::hf_pca9685 , from a package that could not compile). A CTest ( hf_pca9685_install ) builds a find_package() consumer against the install. Added ¶ SetOutputEnable(bool enable) : drives the active-low OE pin (datasheet 7.4) through the port's optional GpioSet(CtrlPin::OE, ...) , ACTIVE to enable the outputs (pin low) and INACTIVE to blank them (pin high). Ports without GpioSet() still compile and get the do-nothing default. Optional port hook DelayUs(uint32_t us) , used for the 500 µs oscillator start-up (see Fixed). Host unit tests ( HF_PCA9685_BUILD_TESTS ) that run the driver against a model of the PCA9685 registers.

Constructor ¶ pca9685 :: PCA9685 < MyI2c > pwm ( & bus , 0x40 ); Argument Type Meaning bus MyI2c* Your port; must outlive the driver. nullptr makes every call fail address uint8_t 7-bit address, 0x40 to 0x7F from A0 to A5 ( Hardware ) Several chips on one bus: one port object, one driver per address. Run-time settings ¶ Setting Call Default Range Retries per register access SetRetries(int) 3 (four attempts) 0 or more Delay between attempts SetRetryDelay(void (*)()) none Any function with no arguments; a capture-less lambda works PWM frequency SetPwmFreq(float) 200 Hz (chip default PRE_SCALE = 30) 24 Hz to 1526 Hz Output driver SetOutputDriverMode(bool) totem pole totem pole or open drain Output inversion SetOutputInvert(bool) not inverted The retry settings live in the driver object; the others are chip registers and survive until a power cycle or a software reset. Chip state after start-up ¶ Register Power-up value After EnsureInitialized() Changed by MODE1 0x11 : SLEEP, ALLCALL 0x20 : awake, AI on, ALLCALL off Reset() , SetPwmFreq() , Sleep() , Wake() MODE2 0x04 : totem pole, change on STOP, OUTNE = 00 unchanged SetOutputDriverMode() , SetOutputInvert() PRE_SCALE 0x1E (30): about 200 Hz unchanged SetPwmFreq() LEDn_ON / LEDn_OFF full off ( LEDn_OFF_H bit 4 = 1) unchanged channel calls Power-up values: Tables 4 to 8 of the datasheet . docs.text: Hardware ¶ What to connect between your MCU and a PCA9685, with which bus settings, and the board-level traps to avoid. All values here come from the PCA9685 datasheet (Rev. 4, 16 April 2015); page numbers refer to it. Pin numbers are for the TSSOP28 package. When they disagree with a breakout board's schematic, the schematic wins. Pins ¶ Pin Signal Function 26 SCL In: I2C clock; pull-up to VDD 27 SDA In/out: I2C data; pull-up to VDD 1-5, 24 A0-A5 In: address bits; no pull-ups, tie each high or low 23 OE In: output enable, active low; no pull-up 25 EXTCLK In: external clock up to 50 MHz; ground it when unused 6-13 LED0-LED7 Out: PWM outputs 15-22 LED8-LED15 Out: PWM outputs 28 VDD Supply, 2.3 V to 5.5 V 14 VSS Ground HVQFN28 pin numbers SCL 23, SDA 24, A0 to A4 26, 27, 28, 1, 2, A5 21, OE 20, EXTCLK 22, LED0 to LED7 3 to 10, LED8 to LED15 12 to 19, VDD 25, VSS 11. The exposed pad is also ground and must be soldered. Source: Table 3, p. 6. Address ¶ The 7-bit address is 1 A5 A4 A3 A2 A1 A0 (Figure 4, p. 8): 0x40 with every address pin low, up to 0x7F with every pin high. Pass it to the constructor: PCA9685<MyI2c> pwm(&bus, 0x41) . Address Use it? Why 0x40 to 0x6F Yes Regular addresses 0x70 No LED All Call address, enabled at power-up: every PCA9685 on the bus answers it 0x71 to 0x77 With care 0x71 , 0x72 and 0x74 are the Sub Call defaults (disabled at power-up) 0x78 to 0x7F No, on a shared bus Reserved by the I2C specification (10-bit addressing, future use) The datasheet counts 62 usable addresses (section 7.1, p. 7). The general-call Software Reset ( 0x00 , data byte 0x06 ) resets every PCA9685 on the bus; the driver does not send it. Bus settings ¶ Setting Value Source Speed Standard mode 100 kHz, Fast mode 400 kHz, Fast-mode Plus 1 MHz Table 15, p. 40 Write START, address + W, register, data bytes, STOP Figure 20, p. 32 Read START, address + W, register, repeated START, address + R, data, STOP Figure 22, p. 33 Multi-byte access The register pointer advances only when MODE1.AI = 1 Table 5, p. 14 Output update On STOP (default, MODE2.OCH = 0) or on ACK Table 6, p. 16 Bus time-out The interface resets if SCL or SDA is held low for at least 25 ms Table 15, note 1 SDA drive 30 mA sink, for buses up to 4000 pF Sections 1 and 2, pp. 1-2 The driver writes a channel as one four-byte transaction starting at LEDn_ON_L and reads single registers. Your port turns each call into exactly one transaction ( Porting ). sequenceDiagram participant H as Host (driver) participant C as PCA9685 Note over H,C: SetPwmFreq(50) H->>C: read MODE1 C-->>H: MODE1 (SLEEP = 0) H->>C: write MODE1 = old | SLEEP (RESTART bit cleared) Note over C: oscillator off, PRE_SCALE writable H->>C: write PRE_SCALE = 121 H->>C: write MODE1 = old (SLEEP = 0) Note over C: oscillator restarts, up to 500 us Note over H: DelayUs(500) H->>C: write MODE1 = old | RESTART Note over C: running channels resume Output stage ¶ The 16 outputs share one configuration in MODE2 (Table 6, p. 16). MODE2 bit Default Effect Driver call OUTDRV (bit 2) 1: totem pole 0: open drain SetOutputDriverMode(bool totem_pole) INVRT (bit 4) 0: not inverted 1: outputs inverted while OE is low SetOutputInvert(bool invert) OCH (bit 3) 0: change on STOP 1: change on ACK none OUTNE[1:0] (bits 1:0) 00: LEDn = 0 while OE is high 01: 1 (totem pole) or high-Z; 1x: high-Z none Totem pole sinks 25 mA and sources 10 mA at 5 V; open drain sinks 25 mA. LEDs with built-in Zener diodes must be driven in open-drain mode (Table 6, note 1). For a servo signal or a logic-level gate driver input use totem pole, INVRT = 0 . OE is active low (section 7.4, p. 27). Low: outputs follow their registers. High: outputs take the OUTNE state, by default low. Tie it low, or wire it to a GPIO and drive it with SetOutputEnable() through your port's GpioSet() ( Porting ). Power ¶ Parameter Min Typ Max Unit Source Supply voltage VDD 2.3 5.5 V Table 14, p. 38 Supply current, operating, no load, f SCL = 1 MHz 6 10 mA Table 14 Standby current (SLEEP, f SCL = 0) 2.2 15.5 µA Table 14 Power-on reset threshold V POR 1.70 2.0 V Table 14 Output current per LEDn pin 25 mA Table 13, p. 38 Total ground current I SS 400 mA Table 13 Operating temperature −40 +85 °C Table 13 To repeat a power-on reset, VDD must fall below 0.2 V (section 7.5, p. 27). Place a 100 nF capacitor between VDD and VSS close to the chip. Loads (servos, LED strings, motors) take their own supply; only the signal and the ground are shared with the PCA9685. Timing that affects the host ¶ Event Time Driver behaviour Oscillator start after MODE1.SLEEP is cleared 500 µs max Reset() , Wake() and SetPwmFreq() wait 500 µs before they return (Table 5, note 2) SLEEP low before writing RESTART 500 µs min Wake() and SetPwmFreq() write RESTART only after the 500 µs wait (section 7.3.1.1, p. 15) OE to output 40 ns to 60 ns n/a (Table 15) Breakout boards ¶ The ESP32 examples run on an ESP32-S3 with a PCA9685 at 0x40 : SDA on GPIO4, SCL on GPIO5, 100 kHz, OE not driven. The pins are in esp32_pca9685_test_config.hpp . Common 16-channel servo breakouts fit the I2C pull-ups, a pull-down on OE and solder jumpers for A0 to A5; check the board's schematic. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 12+ or a current MSVC. CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( pca9685_version.h ). No RTOS, heap or exceptions: every call is noexcept and returns bool . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-pca9685-driver.git external/hf-pca9685-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-pca9685-driver Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ); you do not need it to use the driver. CMake ¶ add_subdirectory ( external/hf-pca9685-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf::pca9685 ) hf::pca9685 is an alias of the hf_pca9685 INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20 ( cxx_std_20 ), so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect HF_PCA9685_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver HF_PCA9685_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host unit tests in tests/ ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/hf-pca9685-driver -B build-pca9685 cmake --install build-pca9685 --prefix /opt/hardfoc find_package ( hf_pca9685 1.0 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/hardfoc target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf::pca9685 ) The headers and the generated pca9685_version.h go to include/hf_pca9685/inc/ and the template implementation the header includes to include/hf_pca9685/src/pca9685.ipp ; the target's include directory is include/hf_pca9685/inc , so the code is the same as with add_subdirectory() : #include "pca9685.hpp" . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing ). ESP-IDF ¶ The ESP-IDF component wrapper is examples/esp32/components/hf_pca9685/ . docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the I2C interface. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls three methods on a class you derive from pca9685::I2cInterface<Self> (in inc/pca9685_i2c_interface.hpp ). The base class uses CRTP: the calls are resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions, no vtable and nothing to allocate. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one PCA9685 object, whose public calls (listed from inc/pca9685.hpp) set the frequency, the channels and the output stage. Each call turns into register reads and writes with retries. The communication interface (I2cInterface in inc/pca9685_i2c_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base that forwards them to your class. The platform port is the only code you write: a class that brings the I2C bus up and moves register bytes over it. Below it is the hardware. Drawn from: inc/pca9685.hpp PCA9685 public calls ; inc/pca9685_i2c_interface.hpp I2cInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you implement ¶ Method Contract EnsureInitialized() Bring the bus up on the first call; return true at once afterwards. false stops the driver from starting Write(addr, reg, data, len) One transaction: START, addr + W, reg , len bytes, STOP. true only if every byte was acknowledged Read(addr, reg, data, len) One transaction: START, addr + W, reg , repeated START, addr + R, len bytes, STOP DelayUs(us) Optional, recommended: wait at least us microseconds. The driver calls it with 500 after it clears MODE1.SLEEP, for the oscillator start-up time (datasheet Table 5, note 2) GpioSet(pin, signal) Optional: drive the OE pin; called by SetOutputEnable() (see below) addr is the 7-bit address; shift it left yourself if your SDK wants the 8-bit form. The driver writes at most four data bytes per call and reads one. The optional methods are found at compile time: a port without them still builds. Without DelayUs() the driver covers the 500 µs start-up with 13 one-byte reads of MODE1, enough at any bus clock up to 1 MHz, so give your port a DelayUs() if its Read() can return without running a bus transaction. I2C port ¶ my_i2c.hpp class MyI2c : public pca9685 :: I2cInterface < MyI2c > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_i2c_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One write transaction: START, address + W, register, data bytes, STOP. bool Write ( uint8_t addr , uint8_t reg , const uint8_t * data , size_t len ) noexcept { uint8_t frame [ 1 + 4 ]; // the driver writes at most 4 data bytes if ( len > sizeof ( frame ) - 1 ) { return false ; } frame [ 0 ] = reg ; for ( size_t i = 0 ; i < len ; ++ i ) { frame [ 1 + i ] = data [ i ]; } return platform_i2c_write ( addr , frame , len + 1 ); } // Register read: START, address + W, register, repeated START, address + R, data, STOP. bool Read ( uint8_t addr , uint8_t reg , uint8_t * data , size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write_read ( addr , & reg , 1 , data , len ); } // Optional: wait at least `us` microseconds. The driver uses it for the 500 us oscillator start-up. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Rules the transfer must follow: One call, one transaction. Never split a channel's four bytes into separate transactions: the chip updates the outputs at the STOP, and the register pointer does not carry over. Repeated START for reads. Write the register byte, then read without a STOP in between (Figure 22 of the datasheet). Return false for a NACK or a bus error. The driver retries and sets the error flags; do not retry in the port as well. Bounded time-outs. A stuck bus should fail the call, not block forever. The chip resets its own interface when SCL or SDA stays low for 25 ms. Clock up to 1 MHz. Start at 100 kHz for bring-up; 400 kHz suits most boards. The OE pin ¶ OE is active low (datasheet section 7.4): low, the outputs follow their registers; high, they take the MODE2.OUTNE state, low by default. If OE is wired to a GPIO, declare GpioSet() in your port and map GpioSignal::ACTIVE (outputs enabled) to a low level: // OE is active low: ACTIVE (outputs enabled) is a LOW level, INACTIVE (blanked) a HIGH level. void GpioSet ( pca9685 :: CtrlPin pin , pca9685 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { if ( pin == pca9685 :: CtrlPin :: OE ) { platform_gpio_write ( OE_GPIO , signal == pca9685 :: GpioSignal :: INACTIVE ); } } SetOutputEnable(true) calls GpioSet(CtrlPin::OE, GpioSignal::ACTIVE) and SetOutputEnable(false) calls it with INACTIVE ; the base class helpers GpioSetActive() and GpioSetInactive() reach your GpioSet() too. A port without GpioSet() inherits a do-nothing default, for boards with OE tied low. The driver never drives OE on its own, so your port can hold the outputs blanked from power-up until the channels are programmed. Reference implementation ¶ The ESP32 examples use esp32_pca9685_bus.hpp : an ESP-IDF i2c_master port that caches the device handle, with a RetryDelay() ( vTaskDelay of 1 ms) that you pass to SetRetryDelay() . Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the port on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over it. Call EnsureInitialized() : true proves a write to MODE1 was acknowledged at your address. Call SetPwmFreq(50.0f) , then GetPrescale() : 121 proves reads and writes both work. Put a scope or logic analyser on LED0 after SetDuty(0, 0.5f) : a 50 % square wave at about 50 Hz. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each PCA9685 one owner task, or guard every call on a driver object with one mutex. Several chips on one bus share the port, so guard the port too.

docs.text: PWM timing ¶ How the PCA9685 makes a PWM waveform: one 12-bit counter, an ON tick and an OFF tick per channel, and a prescaler that sets the period. Read it before you drive servos or need phase-shifted outputs. Values are from the datasheet , sections 7.3.3 to 7.3.5 (pp. 16-25). The counter ¶ Every channel compares one shared counter, running from 0 to 4095 and wrapping, with two 12-bit values: ON tick ( LEDn_ON ): the counter value at which the output goes high. OFF tick ( LEDn_OFF ): the counter value at which it goes low. Duty cycle is (OFF − ON) / 4096 when OFF is after ON, and (4096 − ON + OFF) / 4096 when it wraps. ON and OFF must never be equal (section 7.3.4, p. 25): when you pass equal ticks to SetPwm() or SetAllPwm() , the driver writes the full-OFF bit instead. Call ON tick OFF tick Output SetPwm(ch, 0, 1024) 0 1024 High for ticks 0 to 1023: 25 % SetPwm(ch, 1024, 3072) 1024 3072 50 %, shifted by a quarter period SetPwm(ch, 3072, 1024) 3072 1024 50 %, high across the wrap SetDuty(ch, d) 0 lround(d × 4095) Starts every period at tick 0 SetDuty(ch, 0.0f) 0 bit 12 set Constantly low (full off) SetDuty(ch, 1.0f) bit 12 set 0 Constantly high (full on) SetPwm(ch, t, t) 0 bit 12 set Equal ticks: full off SetChannelFullOn(ch) bit 12 set 0 Constantly high SetChannelFullOff(ch) 0 bit 12 set Constantly low; overrides full on Staggering the ON ticks of channels spreads their switching edges over the period and lowers the current surge on the load supply; SetDuty() always starts at tick 0, so use SetPwm() for that. SetDuty() uses the full-on and full-off bits ( LEDn_ON_H and LEDn_OFF_H bit 4, Table 7, p. 24) for the two ends: 1.0 is constantly high, and any duty that rounds to OFF = 0 (below 1/8190) is constantly low. It never writes ON = OFF. The period ¶ The counter is clocked from the 25 MHz internal oscillator (or EXTCLK) divided by PRE_SCALE + 1 (equation 1, p. 25): PRE_SCALE = round(f_osc / (4096 × f_pwm)) − 1 f_pwm = f_osc / (4096 × (PRE_SCALE + 1)) The chip forces PRE_SCALE to at least 3, which gives the 1526 Hz maximum; 255 gives 23.8 Hz. The driver accepts 24 Hz to 1526 Hz and returns false with Error::OutOfRange outside it. PRE_SCALE can only be written while MODE1.SLEEP = 1, so SetPwmFreq() puts the chip to sleep, writes it and restores MODE1. Requested PRE_SCALE Actual (internal 25 MHz) Tick 50 Hz 121 50.0 Hz 4.88 µs 60 Hz 101 59.8 Hz 4.08 µs 200 Hz (power-up default) 30 196.9 Hz 1.24 µs 1000 Hz 5 1017 Hz 0.24 µs 1526 Hz 3 1526 Hz 0.16 µs The internal oscillator is specified as 25 MHz typical, with no tolerance in the datasheet. When the period matters (servos), measure it once with a scope or logic analyser and scale the pulse widths, or feed EXTCLK from a crystal oscillator. Servo pulses ¶ A hobby servo reads the high time of a pulse repeated every 20 ms (50 Hz). Typical servos centre at 1.5 ms and travel over about 1.0 ms to 2.0 ms; check your servo's datasheet before you go wider. At 50 Hz one tick is 20 ms / 4096 = 4.88 µs, so 1.0 ms to 2.0 ms is about 205 ticks of resolution. // Servo pulse width to PWM ticks: one period is 4096 ticks of 1 / f_pwm. bool set_servo_us ( Driver & pwm , uint8_t channel , float pulse_us , float pwm_hz ) { const float period_us = 1'000'000.0f / pwm_hz ; // 20 000 us at 50 Hz const auto ticks = static_cast < uint16_t > ( pulse_us / period_us * 4096.0f + 0.5f ); return pwm . SetPwm ( channel , 0 , ticks ); // 1500 us at 50 Hz -> 307 ticks } Pulse Ticks at 50 Hz Duty 1.0 ms 205 5.0 % 1.5 ms 307 7.5 % 2.0 ms 410 10.0 % When a change takes effect ¶ A new ON or OFF value is applied at the end of the current low period, so a changing duty cycle produces no glitch (section 7.3.4). With MODE2.OCH = 0 (the default and what the driver leaves), the outputs change at the I2C STOP, so all four bytes of a channel take effect together. docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Centre a hobby servo from your MCU: wire four signals, write a small port class, call three driver functions. Before you power the servo Power servos from their own 5 V supply, not from the PCA9685's VDD or your MCU's regulator, and join the grounds. A stalled servo draws far more than a logic rail can give. 1. Wire it ¶ MCU PCA9685 Notes I2C SCL SCL (pin 26, TSSOP28) Pull-up to VDD; 4.7 kΩ suits 100 kHz and 400 kHz I2C SDA SDA (pin 27) Pull-up to VDD 3.3 V or 5 V VDD (pin 28) 2.3 V to 5.5 V; 100 nF to VSS close to the pin GND VSS (pin 14) Common with the servo supply ground GND or a GPIO OE (pin 23) Active low: tie it low, or drive it to blank all outputs GND A0 to A5, EXTCLK All low: address 0x40 ; EXTCLK must be grounded when unused LED0 (pin 6) Servo signal wire The Hardware page has the full pin list, the address table and the electrical limits. Breakout boards usually fit the pull-ups and tie OE and the address pins already: check yours. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the hf_pca9685 CMake target. Installation covers CMake and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-pca9685-driver.git external/hf-pca9685-driver 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code. It brings the bus up and moves register bytes. Replace the three platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_i2c.hpp class MyI2c : public pca9685 :: I2cInterface < MyI2c > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_i2c_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One write transaction: START, address + W, register, data bytes, STOP. bool Write ( uint8_t addr , uint8_t reg , const uint8_t * data , size_t len ) noexcept { uint8_t frame [ 1 + 4 ]; // the driver writes at most 4 data bytes if ( len > sizeof ( frame ) - 1 ) { return false ; } frame [ 0 ] = reg ; for ( size_t i = 0 ; i < len ; ++ i ) { frame [ 1 + i ] = data [ i ]; } return platform_i2c_write ( addr , frame , len + 1 ); } // Register read: START, address + W, register, repeated START, address + R, data, STOP. bool Read ( uint8_t addr , uint8_t reg , uint8_t * data , size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write_read ( addr , & reg , 1 , data , len ); } // Optional: wait at least `us` microseconds. The driver uses it for the 500 us oscillator start-up. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Porting explains each method and the transfer rules. 4. Centre the servo ¶ main.cpp #include "pca9685.hpp" int center_servo_on_channel_0 ( MyI2c & bus ) { pca9685 :: PCA9685 < MyI2c > pwm ( & bus , 0x40 ); // A0..A5 tied low if ( ! pwm . EnsureInitialized ()) { // 1. bus up, MODE1 reset return -1 ; // wiring, pull-ups or address } if ( ! pwm . SetPwmFreq ( 50.0f )) { // 2. 50 Hz: a 20 ms servo frame return -2 ; } // 3. 1.5 ms high out of 20 ms = 7.5 % duty: servo centre if ( ! pwm . SetDuty ( 0 , 1.5f / 20.0f )) { return -3 ; } return 0 ; } What each step does: EnsureInitialized() calls your port's EnsureInitialized() , then writes MODE1 = 0x20 , which starts the oscillator and turns on register auto-increment. Every other call runs it for you if you skip it. SetPwmFreq(50.0f) writes PRE_SCALE = 121 (the chip only accepts it while asleep; the driver handles that), giving a 20 ms frame. SetDuty(0, 0.075f) sets channel 0 high for 7.5 % of each frame: 1.5 ms, the centre of a typical servo. This example is built by the host CI, so it compiles against the current headers. docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host unit tests against a model of the chip, compiled documentation, ESP32 builds and static analysis, on every pull request. Host unit tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a model of the PCA9685's register interface: power-up register values, PRE_SCALE ignoring writes while the chip is awake, the register pointer advancing only with MODE1.AI set, the RESTART bit and the 500 µs oscillator start-up on a model bus clock, and injected I2C failures. Every transaction the driver sends is logged, so tests check the exact bytes and registers. cmake -S . -B build-host -DHF_PCA9685_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build-host ctest --test-dir build-host --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_driver.cpp Initialisation, retries, frequency and prescaler, channel frames, range checks, sleep, MODE2 tests/mock_pca9685.hpp The register model and transaction log tests/test_harness.hpp A dependency-free test registry and CHECK macros tests/check_install.cmake CTest hf_pca9685_install : installs into a scratch prefix and builds tests/install_consumer/ with find_package(hf_pca9685) Documentation snippets ¶ Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target hf_pca9685_doc_snippets ) with the driver instantiated over the documented port. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see while bringing up a PCA9685, their causes and the fix for each. Start with the error flags of the failing call ( GetErrorFlags() , API guide ): I2cWrite or I2cRead is a bus problem, OutOfRange is a bad argument and nothing was sent. The chip does not answer ¶ EnsureInitialized() returns false with Error::I2cWrite . Cause Check Fix No pull-ups SCL and SDA idle low or slow edges on a scope 4.7 kΩ to VDD on each line (many breakouts fit them) Wrong address An I2C scan of 0x40 to 0x7F Pass the address set by A0 to A5; address pins have no pull-ups and must not float No supply VDD at the chip: 2.3 V to 5.5 V Power it; join the grounds Bus not up Your port's EnsureInitialized() returns false Fix the SDK call; the driver reports it as I2cWrite Address 0x70 Several chips answer at once Use another address: 0x70 is the All Call address Calls succeed but the outputs stay low ¶ Cause Check Fix OE high or floating OE pin level Tie OE low, or call SetOutputEnable(true) with a port that implements GpioSet() ; OE has no internal pull-up Chip asleep MODE1 bit 4 Wake() ; Sleep() and power-up both leave SLEEP set until the driver starts Channel full off LEDn_OFF_H bit 4 SetPwm() with ON ≠ OFF, SetDuty() above 0 or SetChannelFullOn() clear it; SetDuty(ch, 0.0f) and equal ticks set it Load wired to the wrong side Totem pole versus open drain, INVRT Hardware Channel outputs are wrong or do not change ¶ The driver writes each channel as one four-byte transaction starting at LEDn_ON_L and relies on MODE1.AI (register auto-increment) to move the register pointer through LEDn_ON_H , LEDn_OFF_L and LEDn_OFF_H (Table 5, p. 14). Reset() sets AI and every later MODE1 write of the driver keeps it. Cause Check Fix Port splits or truncates the transfer A logic analyser on the bus: one START, five data bytes, one STOP One call, one transaction ( Porting ) Your own MODE1 write cleared AI MODE1 bit 5 Keep bit 5 set in raw MODE1 writes, or call Reset() again The frequency is off ¶ Cause Check Fix Out of range SetPwmFreq() returns false , Error::OutOfRange 24 Hz to 1526 Hz only Prescaler rounding GetPrescale() , then f = 25 MHz / (4096 × (PRE_SCALE + 1)) PWM timing Oscillator tolerance Measure the period on a scope Scale your pulse widths, or clock the chip from EXTCLK Servos jitter or move to the wrong place ¶ Cause Fix Servo powered from the logic supply A separate 5 V supply sized for the stall current of all servos; common ground Pulse width beyond the servo's range Stay within the servo datasheet's range, often 1.0 ms to 2.0 ms Frequency not 50 Hz, or not measured SetPwmFreq(50.0f) , then check the 20 ms frame on a scope SetPwmFreq() called repeatedly It stops the oscillator each time: call it once at start-up Intermittent I2C errors ¶ Cause Fix Long wires, slow edges Lower the clock to 100 kHz; stronger pull-ups; shorter wiring Noise from motors or servos Route I2C away from load wiring; decouple VDD with 100 nF at the chip Retries without a pause SetRetryDelay() with a 1 ms delay between attempts Two tasks using the driver One owner task, or one mutex around the driver and the port ( Porting )
